checks: A convex facet-speed maximum which is odd on a linear subspace is also concave there, so the speed, D and all individual contact responses are linear. The reversal of the contact minimum is −α−σ.
One-group non-descent applies in both directions; the volume and scale terms cancel on addition and give L+L^-≤0.
Using the two hinge formulas gives max(v,c)+max(−v,−c)=|v−c| on the inside and min(0,v+c)+min(0,−v−c)=−|v+c| on the outside. Other terms cancel under (h,r)→(−h,−r).

R_j(−h,−r_j)=−L+E_j, so inverse displacement from −r_j to the threshold at −L is the signed inverse-derivative integral. Forward slopes are positive and finite; breakpoints do not affect the integral.

The reversed weighted inverse at −L is at least its value at L^- and adding α gives ≥−σ. When σ=0, simultaneous E_j>0 contradicts this. Fixed choices of the three relevant branch evaluations give a linear comparison.
Matched 6714ecb94bcabe5f §§5–6 (5)–(8), including the one-group and odd-subspace restrictions.

dependencies.hypotheses: The draft assumes the same actual local minimum and fixed-normal paths as the predecessor, with precisely one cover group. Both signs are admissible, and the predecessor gives unique exact equalization and the required one-group non-descent inequality.

overlap.comparison: Provides exact per-cap inverse slopes, but does not compare the forward and reverse common losses at a one-group minimum or retain the exact contact spread.

readability: The signed integral is in the loss variable, not the threshold variable. Its limits are ordered as −L+E_j to −L.
review_method: Independent cold proof read of the frozen candidate, with original-source, dependency and scope checks.
summary: On the odd-speed subspace the reversed contact budget is exactly minus the old maximum response. The strict monotonicity of the inverse loss gives the weighted threshold correction and the single-contact sign consequence.
